text:
maya: Heads-up - CloudGauge sent a fresh quote for their inference cost platform. Can procurement weigh in on license flexibility?

sam: link to quote: https://cloudgauge.example/quote/CG-2026-04 — they propose a hybrid model: committed throughput + burst credits.

julian: @maya thanks. Do we have our current baseline (tokens + embeddings) handy? I want to check cost delta before engaging on T&Cs.

ev: Quick numbers: avg 120M generation tokens/mo, 8M embedding items/mo. Peak day 6x baseline.

maya: OK - vendor sent a sample price table. Paste from quote:
```
Committed Tier A: 100M tokens/mo = $1,200/mo (effective $12 / 1M tokens)
Burst Credits: $18 / 1M tokens when bursts exceed commitment
Embeddings: $0.003 per vector, 5% discount with commitment
Annual support fee: $6k (optional)
```

julian: That committed rate is attractive vs current PAYG (we're at ~ $15/1M tokens). But we need license flexibility: ability to scale down mid-year without penalty, and pro-rated commit adjustments.

alison: Legal: must confirm audit & data residency language. CloudGauge's default clause allows vendor audits and access to usage logs; we need to restrict to summary-level reporting and require 48h notice. Also push for breach remediation timelines.

cloudgauge_sales: thanks everyone! we can add pro-rated commit adjustments (one change per quarter) and limit audits to sample reports. happy to send redline.

maya: Good. Two other procurement asks: 1) termination for convenience with 60-day notice and refund for unused committed credits; 2) SLA credits tied to 99.95% availability for inference endpoints.

cloudgauge_sales: we usually do 30-day termination and no refunds on committed months. SLA 99.9% is our standard, but we can escalate for enterprise.

sam: Given our peak factor, burst credits are important. Can we ask for lower burst price if we commit to a 12-month min? e.g., $14/1M for bursts capped at 2x monthly baseline?

julian: Also flag exportability of usage logs in structured JSON on a daily cadence - needed for our billing reconciliation.

alison: Add a clause: vendor cannot use our aggregate telemetry for benchmarking their public product without anonymization and opt-out.

procurement-bot: FYI - we have an open PO template for vendor commits. Recommend attaching estimated monthly spend + 20% buffer.

maya: Next steps: Julian to request redline with pro-rate & 60-day termination; Sam/Evan to produce a 3-month projected usage file (tokens + embeddings + 95th percentile peak) for pricing negotiation; Alison to draft minimal audit/data use language.

julian: I'll request redline today and ask for a 5% discount on bursts for a 12-mo commit. Also querying their penalty for exceeding committed throughput (do they throttle or bill bursts automatically?).

ev: If they throttle, that would break some latency SLOs - must avoid. Ask for auto-billing of bursts instead of throttling and cap on throttled requests only in emergency.

cloudgauge_sales: noted. I'll confirm billing behavior vs throttling and push for a burst discount for 12mo. Expect updated redline by EOD Friday.

maya: Great - please copy procurement thread and tag me when redline arrives. Quick note: if they won't refund unused credits, ask for rollover up to 3 months.

sam: +1 on rollover. Also request a small pilot (1 month) at commit-to-burst blended pricing so infra can validate bucket behavior under load.

maya: Thanks all. If vendor acknowledges these three levers (pro-rate adjustments, 60d termination + refund/rollover, burst discount), procurement can take to execs for approval.

julian: will update here when I have the redline.

cloudgauge_sales: redline ETA Friday 17:00 PT.

maya: :thumbsup:
